title: PDRN Serum
h1: Vegan PDRN Serum — Clean, K-Beauty-Grade Brightening
intro: PDRN serum is the K-beauty brightening treatment everyone's talking about — and almost every version on the market is made from salmon DNA. Ours isn't. Leaf & Bird's vegan PDRN serum delivers the same clinical brightening, minus the fish. Non-animal-sourced polydeoxyribonucleotide, clean actives, honest ingredients. Formulated for health-conscious moms who read labels and refuse to compromise.

body_modules.heading: What makes our PDRN different
body_modules.html:
Vegan-sourced polydeoxyribonucleotide

Most PDRN on the market — including the K-beauty serums you've probably seen recommended — is derived from salmon sperm DNA. That's the commercial standard, and it's why finding a truly vegan PDRN feels nearly impossible. Our polydeoxyribonucleotide is non-animal-sourced, full stop. Same bioactive class of molecule, same support for fibroblast activity and barrier resilience — without the fish origin. For health-conscious moms, this isn't a small distinction. It's the whole reason this serum exists.

Acetyl Hexapeptide-8 (Argireline): the Botox-alternative peptide co-hero

Acetyl Hexapeptide-8, better known as Argireline, is a signaling peptide that works at the neuromuscular junction to visibly soften expression lines over time. It's often called a "topical Botox alternative" — not because the mechanism is identical, but because the end result (relaxed-looking expression lines) is achieved without needles, downtime, or synthetic neurotoxins. No irritation, no photosensitivity, no retinol trade-offs. Pairs seamlessly with PDRN for a one-two brightening and smoothing effect.

Clean formulation with honest trade-offs

We know our audience checks EWG ratings and reads every ingredient. So we'll say it plainly: this formula contains phenoxyethanol, a non-paraben preservative required in any water-based product to prevent bacterial and mold growth. We use it at a low, EWG-acceptable concentration (typically rated 1–2). Some crunchy-mom shoppers prefer to avoid it entirely — we respect that choice. We'd rather earn your trust with transparency than lose it by hiding anything. See the FAQ below for the full context.

body_modules.heading: The active system
body_modules.html:
Every ingredient in the formula earns its place. Here's what the actives do and why they matter:

  • Polydeoxyribonucleotide (PDRN) — non-salmon-derived: The headline active. PDRN is a bioactive polynucleotide that supports fibroblast signaling — the cellular pathway behind collagen synthesis and skin repair. Applied topically, it promotes a brighter, firmer-looking complexion and helps restore barrier resilience over time. Ours is non-animal-sourced, making it one of the only vegan PDRN formulations available anywhere.
  • Acetyl Hexapeptide-8 (Argireline): A peptide that mimics the N-terminal end of SNAP-25, moderating the neuromuscular signals that cause repetitive muscle contractions. The result: expression lines visibly soften with consistent use. No irritation, no sun sensitivity — just cumulative improvement.
  • Sodium Hyaluronate: Low-molecular-weight hyaluronic acid that penetrates into the upper skin layers, binding water molecules and delivering immediate visible plumping. The form matters here — Sodium Hyaluronate absorbs faster and more effectively than higher-molecular-weight HA.
  • Panthenol (Vitamin B5): A proven barrier-supporting ingredient that converts to pantothenic acid in the skin, aiding moisture retention and soothing reactive or stressed skin. Especially valuable for hormonally sensitive skin types common in the postpartum and perimenopause window.
  • Sodium PCA: A natural moisturizing factor (NMF) component — one of the skin's own humectants. It draws water to the surface and helps lock it in, giving the formula its comfortable, non-sticky finish while reinforcing the barrier from the inside out.

body_modules.heading: Your AM + PM routine
body_modules.html:
Pair the PDRN Brightening Serum with the Peptide Eye Gel-Cream for a complete K-beauty-inspired brightening routine.

  1. AM — Cleanse: Start with a gentle, low-pH cleanser. Pat skin dry — don't rub.
  2. AM — PDRN Serum: Apply 2–4 pumps of the Vegan PDRN Brightening Serum to face and neck. Massage gently until fully absorbed. Let it settle 30–60 seconds.
  3. AM — Peptide Eye Gel-Cream: Apply a pea-sized amount of the Peptide Eye Gel-Cream using your ring finger, tapping gently along the orbital bone. The peptide-rich eye formula targets crow's feet and under-eye hollows while the serum works on the full face.
  4. AM — Moisturizer + SPF: Seal with your preferred moisturizer and a broad-spectrum SPF 30+. PDRN and Argireline have no photosensitivity risk, but daily SPF is non-negotiable for any brightening routine.
  5. PM — Cleanse: Double-cleanse if you wore SPF or makeup. Pat dry.
  6. PM — PDRN Serum → Eye Gel-Cream → Night Cream: Repeat the serum and eye gel-cream steps. Follow with a rich night cream or tallow balm to lock in the actives and support overnight repair. This is where PDRN works hardest — skin renewal peaks while you sleep.

body_modules.html:

But she's also the person who googled "is PDRN salmon-derived" at 11pm and then abandoned her cart when she found out it was. She wants the brightening results. She might be postpartum and navigating melasma for the first time. When she finds a brand that's honest — that admits what's in the bottle and why — she becomes a loyal customer. That's exactly who we formulated this for.

body_modules.heading: What you won't find
body_modules.html:
We mean it when we say clean. Here's what this formula leaves out — and one thing it includes that we want you to know about:

  • No salmon DNA
  • No animal derivatives
  • No parabens
  • No sulfates
  • No synthetic fragrance
  • No PEGs
  • No retinol
  • No phthalates

One honest disclosure: This formula does contain phenoxyethanol as a preservative — necessary to keep any water-based product safe from bacterial growth. We use it at low, EWG-accepted concentrations and we'd rather tell you upfront than hide it in a footnote. See the FAQ section for the full context on why it's here and how to weigh that for your routine.

faq_json.question: Is this PDRN serum vegan?
faq_json.answer: Yes. Leaf & Bird's PDRN serum uses non-animal-sourced polydeoxyribonucleotide — no salmon, no fish DNA, no animal derivatives of any kind. The entire formula is 100% vegan. This is genuinely rare: the overwhelming majority of commercial PDRN, including in popular K-beauty serums and clinical injectables, is derived from salmon sperm DNA. Ours is not, which is exactly what makes it worth talking about.

faq_json.question: How is this different from Korean brand PDRN serums like Medicube or Rejuvenex?
faq_json.answer: Popular K-beauty PDRN serums — including those from Medicube, Rejuvenex, and most clinical-grade Korean brands — use salmon-derived PDRN. That's the industry standard and has been since PDRN was first developed for dermatological use in Korea. Leaf & Bird uses non-salmon-derived, vegan PDRN, giving you the same bioactive class of ingredient without the fish origin. For vegans, ethically-oriented shoppers, or moms who just prefer to know exactly what's in their products, that's a meaningful difference.

faq_json.question: Can I use PDRN serum with retinol, vitamin C, or niacinamide?
faq_json.answer: PDRN is a low-irritation active that layers well with most serums. Niacinamide pairs well — both support brightness and barrier health. Vitamin C can be used alongside PDRN; apply it first if your formula is low-pH. Retinol is compatible, but our serum already contains Argireline peptide for line-softening, so many users find they don't need retinol in the same routine at all.

faq_json.question: Is this PDRN serum safe during pregnancy?
faq_json.answer: We always recommend checking with your OB or midwife before adding any new active to your routine during pregnancy or breastfeeding. That said, this formula does not contain retinoids, retinol, salicylic acid, or hydroquinone — the ingredients most commonly flagged during pregnancy. It does contain phenoxyethanol and Acetyl Hexapeptide-8; your provider can help you assess those for your situation. Many of our customers use this serum throughout pregnancy, but the call is yours and your provider's to make.

faq_json.question: How long until I see results from a PDRN serum?
faq_json.answer: You'll typically notice improved hydration and skin softness within the first few applications. For visible brightening, tone evening, and fine-line softening, most users see meaningful change at the 4–6 week mark with consistent twice-daily use. PDRN and Argireline peptide both build results cumulatively — the longer you use them, the more your skin banks the benefit. Think of this as a 90-day investment, not a 3-day fix.

faq_json.question: Does PDRN serum replace retinol?
faq_json.answer: Different mechanism, meaningful overlap in results. Retinol accelerates cell turnover but brings peeling, redness, and photosensitivity for many users. PDRN supports fibroblast signaling and barrier repair, while Argireline in our formula softens expression lines via a peptide pathway — no irritation, no sun sensitivity. Many users find our PDRN serum delivers comparable visible improvement without the trade-offs. They can coexist; alternate evenings if you use both.

faq_json.question: Why is vegan PDRN so rare?
faq_json.answer: Supply chain and biotech. Commercial PDRN has been manufactured from salmon sperm DNA since its origins in Korean dermatology clinics — the process is well-established and cost-efficient at scale. Non-animal-sourced PDRN requires alternative biotech synthesis: less common, more expensive, harder to source. That's why Leaf & Bird's vegan PDRN serum sits in a very small category globally. If you've been searching for a salmon-free option, you've probably come up empty until now.
